key_insight: Cedalion is an open-source Python framework that unifies model-based and data-driven analysis for multimodal fNIRS and DOT, enabling end-to-end, reproducible pipelines from lab recordings to wearable everyday data. It bridges neuroimaging and modern ML workflows for scalable, interoperable analysis.
problem_solved: Current fNIRS/DOT tools are fragmented across platforms, hindering reproducibility, multimodal integration, and seamless incorporation into ML pipelines for real-world wearable neuroimaging.
method: Modular Python framework providing standardized steps: data ingestion, preprocessing, forward/inverse model-based DOT reconstruction, and ML-ready feature extraction.
Native support for multimodal synchronization (e.g., motion, EEG, physiological sensors) and APIs to integrate with ML libraries (PyTorch, scikit-learn) for end-to-end modeling.
Open-source tooling with reproducible workflow support (containers/notebooks, standardized formats, metadata) to ensure interoperability and scalable deployment from lab to field.
impact: AI/ML practitioners gain a reproducible, interoperable toolbox to develop and validate models on realistic multimodal neuroimaging datasets, accelerating research on wearable brain monitoring and ML-driven biomarkers.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: data acquisition (lab & wearable) → preprocessing → DOT/fNIRS reconstruction → ML modeling & evaluation
Before/after comparison: fragmented toolchain vs unified Cedalion workflow (icons for reproducibility, interoperability)
Multimodal sensor schematic: fNIRS + DOT + motion/EEG overlayed on head icon to show synchronization
Example outputs: reconstructed brain activation maps and a t-SNE/embedding showing ML-derived features
paper_title: Cedalion Tutorial: A Python-based framework for comprehensive analysis of multimodal fNIRS & DOT from the lab to the everyday world
paper_authors: E. Middell, L. Carlton, S. Moradi, T. Codina, T. Fischer
